reflections.summary: Lost to Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice under Tailwind, and the loss was set up at preview: of the four I brought, Garchomp was 2x weak to Fairy, Whimsicott was a 1-HP-after-crit body, and Basculegion/Floette took full neutral spread damage, so every turn after Staraptor's Tailwind was pure chip in their favour. Megaing Floette was the wrong stone use — it is slower than their whole squad, its Fairy STABs are neutral into Sylveon and resisted by Arcanine-Hisui, and Mega-Raichu-Y's No Guard Zap Cannon paralysed it on turn 2, turning my Mega into dead weight. Piloting compounded this on turn 3: I Protected Floette while Garchomp sat exposed to Hyper Voice and died, giving up my second attacker for free, and on turn 4 Basculegion spent its Aqua Jet finishing a 23% Staraptor instead of removing Sylveon, so the Hyper Voice engine never stopped and cleaned Whimsicott/Basculegion/Floette in three turns while I never threatened Sylveon at all.
reflections.adjustment: Kill the Hyper Voice engine first: bring at least one Fairy-resist body (Steel/Fire/Poison) alongside Basculegion so their spread move isn't free, do not Mega Floette, and once Sylveon is on the field commit Basculegion's Wave Crash (83-160%, a roll to OHKO) into it rather than mopping up a chipped Staraptor — chip damage on their leads is worth far less than removing the cleaner.
